title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
summary: StreamEmbed replaces per-screenshot full visual encoding (and OCR-only indexing) with incremental embedding: spatial token pruning skips blocks repeated from neighbors, temporal KV reuse caches keys and values for blocks unchanged across frames, and a learned adapter corrects the resulting fidelity loss. The cost is added system complexity, KV cache storage per frame, and a small adapter that must be trained to preserve parity with full-screenshot embeddings. It can fail when screens change abruptly or globally (video playback, scrolling, app switches), where pixel-diff assumptions break, reuse hit rates collapse, and latency regresses toward full encoding while the adapter may not fully compensate.
rationale: The technique directly fits a single-GPU real-time indexing workload and shows a quantified latency gain with maintained accuracy, but its benefits depend on the incremental-change statistics of the reader's actual screen stream and require validating the adapter on their own data before production adoption.
technique: Incremental visual embedding via pixel-diff-guided pruning and temporal KV reuse

claims.statement: StreamEmbed replaces per-screenshot full visual encoding (and OCR-only indexing) with incremental embedding: spatial token pruning skips blocks repeated from neighbors, temporal KV reuse caches keys and values for blocks unchanged across frames, and a learned adapter corrects the resulting fidelity loss. The cost is added system complexity, KV cache storage per frame, and a small adapter that must be trained to preserve parity with full-screenshot embeddings. It can fail when screens change abruptly or globally (video playback, scrolling, app switches), where pixel-diff assumptions break, reuse hit rates collapse, and latency regresses toward full encoding while the adapter may not fully compensate.

Encodes up to 3.7x faster than full-screenshot encoding without sacrificing accuracy, and improves accuracy over OCR-based indexing by up to 6.3 Recall@10 points at matched latency; a year of simulated screenshots indexes in 0.13 GB of RAM.
